items.title: Gerald Wiggins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 2, 1995
items.q: Gerald can be heard at festivals and concerts across the country and still records with such artists as Red Holloway and Clark Terry.

ctx.x: Pianist Gerald Wiggins has been a fixture in the West Coast jazz scene for many years. Originally from New York, born in 1922, Gerald first made his mark with Les Hite, Louis Armstrong and Benny Carter. His West Coast work included stints in the film and recording studios and he accompanied numerous jazz vocalists, including Lena Horne and Kay Starr. Gerald can be heard at festivals and concerts across the country and still records with such artists as Red Holloway and Clark Terry.
Gerald was interviewed in Los Angeles on September 2, 1995 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Gerald Wiggins is a marvelous accompanist, a great pianist, and underrated like hell.

ctx.x: Gerald Wiggins is a marvelous accompanist, a great pianist, and underrated like hell. He’ll play – he’ll swing you into bad health. He’s a good player, and his little boy plays great bass, little Junior, whatever his name is.
Tell me about your time with Gerry Mulligan.
